title: Choose model-qualified PI response targets
equipment: Recirculating water heater, buffer tank, and continuous belt dryer
physicalPurpose: Choose PI speed and robustness deliberately for self-regulating and integrating industrial processes.
objective: Calculate and validate Fast, Balanced, and Robust PI candidates from eligible models while keeping every candidate unapplied.

simplifications: Tank valve lag reduced to an effective delay for tuning

baseline.limitation: A critical-point estimate does not expose a deliberate closed-loop speed-versus-robustness target or distinguish self-regulating from integrating tuning equations.

change.decision: Retain all model-qualified candidates and validation evidence for review; do not select or apply a winner in the PLC program.

acceptance.window: 210 s through 220 s after settling qualification
210 s through 220 s after settling qualification
210 s through 220 s after settling qualification

abortPredicates: Any required signal is missing, stale, forced, nonfinite, or has bad quality
Any process value or applied output leaves its declared hard limit
The model identity, sample interval, event schedule, or seed differs from the reviewed experiment
safety.restorationMode: Restore the heater setpoint to 20 degC; the program restores the linked tank and dryer setpoints to 50 and 40 percent before another candidate
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer and responsible plant operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: This lesson cannot authorise physical excitation or parameter application
Physical use requires independent topology, model, hazard, limit, interlock, and rollback review plus explicit immediate approval

video.viewerOutcome: Calculate and validate transparent PI response targets for self-regulating and integrating processes without silently applying gains.

learning.context: Three independent simulated industrial plants execute the same shipped PI controller against different model classes.
learning.reason: A feedback-relay estimate does not provide a deliberate response-speed target or the correct integrating-process tuning equation.
theory: Desired closed-loop time controls the speed-versus-robustness tradeoff.
Self-regulating gain is a steady output-to-input ratio, while integrating rate gain is output change per input per second.
SIMC produces transparent PI parameters from an eligible model and is not model-predictive control.
learning.workedPrediction: Calculate Fast, Balanced, and Robust Kp, Ti, and parallel Ki for the heater, tank, and dryer before running any candidate.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, plant identity, model class, parameter units, operating points, signal quality, sample interval, limits, events, seed, and candidate state.
Declare response and robustness measures before validation.
learning.baseline: The relay lesson provides one critical point but no explicit model-based response target.
learning.change: Calculate model-eligible SIMC PI candidates for three declared response targets.
learning.comparison: Change only the response target while holding each plant, initial state, event schedule, sampling, limits, and seed constant.
learning.validation: Compare nominal, 20-percent gain increase, and 50-percent effective-delay increase; classify invalid runs before ranking measures.
learning.explanation: A larger response target lowers feedback gain and provides more tolerance to lag and delay, while the integrating tank requires rate-gain equations.
learning.transfer: Retain qualified candidates as unapplied evidence; Lesson 45 adds explicit stability analysis.
